records.region: Neuquén Province, Argentina: arid plateau ravine and southeastward dry-channel valley ending in a fan and saline-playa depression.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Four original imagery views geographically cover the complete selected corridor and receiving playa, but imagery contains no hydronym. Four independent naming-publication attempts yielded no readable substantive material. Discovery snippets are not used to assign a name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The route begins in a western plateau ravine, follows a dry valley east and then southeast through multiple side-valley joins, leaves confinement at a sandy fan and continues into the same broad receiving playa. No supplied tributary fragment or separate lake-reservoir connector is present.
records.completion_scope: Every stored part and join is covered by overlapping original views, including the southern fan continuation, entry onto the playa, final northeastward bend and actual selected ending. Diffuse wash traces and absence of a continuous wet channel on the terminal fan/playa do not constitute a missing geographic transfer. A name, precise bank, active flow at acquisition time, operational hydraulic link or exact modern mouth is not inferred.
records.supported_name_scope: No selected-reach or whole-route natural-river name established.

scope_limits: The river or individual reach names remain unestablished by actually read substantive material.
The terminal depression name is likewise not independently established; it is not assigned to the river.
The lower fan includes aeolian sandy hummocks, vegetation and diffuse wash traces. The reading establishes the receiving landform setting, not one continuously active modern channel.
The unlabelled imagery mosaic has no locally verified source-scene dates. Dry appearance is not proof of permanent absence of flow.
Roads and gridded land-use markings occur near the lower corridor/playa; no construction type, operator, reservoir identity or current water-management operation is asserted.
